{"body":"Implements recursive plugin dependency resolution. Dependencies of dependencies are planned before any download, verified against the plan, and installed as one journaled operation that rolls back on failure.

String dependencies such as `"dependencies": ["foo"]` are required. A missing or failing required dependency aborts the install and leaves nothing new on disk. Optional dependencies use the object form `{"plugin": "foo", "required": false}`. A failing optional branch rolls back to its own savepoint and is reported, while the rest of the install continues.

The planner selects one version per plugin. An installed plugin is retained when it is unpinned, at the pin, or newer than the pin (with a warning), and upgraded when older than the pin. An absent plugin gets the pinned version or the latest compatible one. A repeated visit with a higher pin, a different host, or a suite-component target fails the plan.

Settings for dependencies are passed with `--dependency-config plugin.key=value`. Required settings are prompted before any mutation. Noninteractive runs abort before mutation and print the exact argument to pass. `install --upgrade` on a current plugin repairs missing or outdated dependencies.

Published directories, replaced checkpoints, `.pth` files, and config keys are journaled and undone in reverse order. Checkpoints that cannot be restored are kept under `.plugins-trash/recovery-*`, which trash sweeping never removes. Python environment changes are not rolled back and error messages say so. Python is probed and pip runs only when an installed or upgraded plugin declares requirements. Requirements of retained installed plugins join the combined pip check as constraints.

`bundle create` includes the required dependency closure, planned against an empty installed set, accepts unpinned references, and reports omitted optional dependencies. `uninstall` reports installed plugins and suite components that depend on the target and keeps companion dependencies that another installed plugin still declares. Repository indexes publish expanded suite roots only.

Six independent review passes were run against the plan and against `main` behavior. Every finding was fixed with a test.

`just lint` is clean. The full test tree passes with both `HCLI_CURRENT_IDA_PYTHON_EXE` and `IDAPYTHON_VENV_EXECUTABLE` unset, except `test_verify_pip_can_install_packages`, which fails the same way on `main` in that environment because the system interpreter is externally managed.
